name.text: CHEM_U03_L07_QZ Q01 - Nomenclature and Chemical Communication

questiontext.text:
MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.BON.03

Stimulus:

FormulaCompound typeName rule
NaClionic, fixed-charge metalsodium chloride
FeCl3ionic, variable-charge metaliron(III) chloride
CO2molecularcarbon dioxide

Question: Which conclusion is best supported by the Naming decision table?

generalfeedback.text: Use the embedded stimulus first, then connect the evidence to the bonding, formula, property, or nomenclature rule.

answer.text: Roman numerals show how many atoms are in every molecular compound.

feedback.text: This choice applies the wrong naming system or misuses Roman numerals and prefixes.

answer.text: CO2 is named carbon oxide because prefixes are never used in chemistry names.

feedback.text: This choice applies the wrong naming system or misuses Roman numerals and prefixes.

answer.text: CO2 uses a prefix because it is a molecular compound made from nonmetals.

feedback.text: The stimulus shows that accurate naming begins by classifying the compound type and then applying the matching rule.

answer.text: The formula type does not matter when choosing a naming rule.
